messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation did not significantly change depression ratings compared with placebo in healthy young adults.
Sentence: "Despite significant increases in vitamin D status in the active group, no significant changes were observed in working memory (F = 1.09; p = 0.30), response inhibition (F = 0.82; p = 0.37), cognitive flexibility (F = 1.37; p = 0.24) or secondary outcomes."
Measured as: ratings of depression
Population: Healthy young adults recruited at The University of Queensland
Intervention: Vitamin D 5000 IU cholecalciferol capsule daily for six weeks
Comparator: Identical placebo capsule
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 128
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation reduced depression severity (BDI-II) more than placebo in patients with mild to moderate depression.
Sentence: "At the end point, statistically significant changes were observed only in intervention group as compared with controls including increased 25(OH)D concentration (+ 40.83 ± 28.57 vs. + 5.14 ± 23.44 nmol L-1, P < 0.001) and decreased depression severity (-11.75 ± 6.40 vs. -3.61 ± 10.40, P = 0.003)."
Measured as: depression severity (Beck Depression Inventory-II)
Population: 56 patients aged 18-60 years with mild to moderate depression
Intervention: cholecalciferol 50,000 IU every 2 weeks for 8 weeks
Comparator: placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 56
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
